@@ -3,7 +3,7 @@ "info": { "title": "Victual REST API", "description": "Authentication uses one of the credentials below. Which one is accepted depends on the operation.

**API key.** Send an API key you manage [here](PlaceHolderManageApiKeysUrl) in the *VICTUAL-API-KEY* header. Add the optional *VICTUAL-API-KEY-TYPE* header to narrow which key types may match; it can only remove authority, never add it. A read-only key is limited to GET, HEAD and OPTIONS and gets **403** on anything else; it also gets **403** on three GET operations that write: GET /calendar/ical/sharing-link, GET /stock/barcodes/external-lookup/{barcode} and GET /print/shoppinglist/thermal. A general API key is never accepted in the query string; the calendar secret on GET /calendar/ical is the only query-string credential.

**Session cookie.** Requests from the frontend authenticate with the *victual_session* cookie. On API routes, a request authenticated by the session cookie other than GET, HEAD or OPTIONS is refused with **403** when its Origin header (or its Referer header, if there is no Origin) names another origin. A request with neither header is allowed. Requests authenticated by an API key rather than the session cookie are exempt.

**Calendar secret.** The calendar feed link carries a calendar key in the *secret* query parameter. It is accepted on GET /calendar/ical only. GET /calendar/ical/sharing-link does not accept it, and no other operation does.

**Label worker, verifier and renderer keys.** These use the same *VICTUAL-API-KEY* header but are accepted only on the label worker and renderer operations that name them. On those operations user API keys, session cookies and a disabled-authentication setup are refused with **401**. POST /labels/pair is public.

**Deployment modes.** These are not credentials. With reverse-proxy authentication the server takes the user's identity from a header set by the proxy. In dev, demo and prerelease modes, in an embedded install, and with authentication disabled, requests run as the default user without a credential, except on the label worker and renderer operations above.

**Dates and times.** Every instant this API stores or sends is RFC 3339 in UTC with exactly six fractional digits - `2026-10-04T18:30:00.000000Z` - typed *format: date-time* (ADR-0027 decision 2, issue #650). The fixed width is part of the contract: text order is chronological order, so two values may be compared as strings. The one exception is *time_local* on the system time endpoint, the same instant with the server's offset (`2026-10-04T14:30:00.000000-04:00`). Fields whose column is a SQL DATE are calendar dates, typed *format: date* and written `YYYY-MM-DD`; they are never converted between zones. Days the server computes - due today, overdue, expiring in N days - are days in the server's configured time zone. A value sent without an offset - to the three write fields *tracked_time* and *done_time*, to a generic entity write, or as a `query[]` comparison - is a wall clock in the server's configured zone: a repeated hour names the earlier instant, and a skipped hour is refused with **400**. Send an offset to name any instant unambiguously.
